newsitem.title: GERMANY: Wall St, dollar continues to buoy German shares.
newsitem.headline: Wall St, dollar continues to buoy German shares.

text.p: German shares remained on the record-setting trail in early trade on Friday, as a further overnight rally on Wall Street and the persistently firm dollar continued to buoy the market.
The 30-share DAX index was up 31.41 points at 3,260.89 after the first hour of floor trading, mainly playing catch-up with a sharp advance in late screen-based trade on Thursday.
However many dealers were still suggesting that a significant downward consolidation was on the cards for a market that has seen an apparently unstoppable surge for weeks.
"You get the feeling a lot of the funds are already fully invested," said one dealer.
Dealers said the extent of the consolidation depended largely on the strength of the dollar, suggesting that if the U.S. currency was weak, any fall could be significant.

The dollar was trading just below 1.69 marks, towards the top end of the range expected by currency dealers ahead of a range of U.S. data due later today, including producer prices and industrial production.

Banks were in the spotlight, generally posting gains, after Morgan Stanley upgraded it outlook for their stock while Moody's Investor Service said it had placed Dresdner Bank's AAA credit rating under review.
Dresdner was up 20 pfennigs at 54.55 marks, as it said it did not expect any refinancing problems even if Moody's went ahead with the downgrade.

Metallgesellscahft rose 1.37 marks to 34.200 marks after Thursday's late news that it had decided not to take on a 49.99 percent stake in industrial holding company AGIV -- a move which the market feared would have diluted its profits.

Utility Viag dipped one mark to 708 marks after posting a rise in 1996 profit that was broadly in line with expectations, but prompted some shift of interest to rivals in the sector whose earnings position is still unclear.
